response.response:
{
  "research_question": "To determine if there are statistically significant differences in mouse navigation performance metrics (Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion) across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham).",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target, Average Speed, and Path Efficiency: Conduct a one-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as the fixed factor. H0: mu_i = mu for all i (no difference in means); H1: At least one mu_i differs.",
    "For Success: Conduct a one-way ANOVA as a continuous dependent variable (or verify normality, else use Kruskal-Wallis). H0: Mean success rate is equal across groups.",
    "For AD: Conduct a one-way ANOVA. H0: Mean angular dispersion is equal across groups.",
    "Check homogeneity of variances (Levene's Test) for all continuous models."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Normality of residuals: Assess via Shapiro-Wilk test and Q-Q plots for each response variable after fitting the ANOVA model.",
    "Homogeneity of variance: Assess via Levene's Test or Bartlett's Test given the large sample size imbalance (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505); Welch's ANOVA is preferred if heterogeneity is detected.",
    "Independence of observations: Verified by experimental design (each mouse appears once per paradigm in the filtered data view, n=76655 total).",
    "Linearity and Additivity: Standard ANOVA assumptions, though less critical with random effects fixed here; focus is on group deviations.",
    "Skewness check: Success is bounded [0,1]; Time-to-Target has moderate skew (SD/Mean ratio <1 but min=0); AD is bounded [0,1]. Transformations (log/arcsine) may be needed if residuals are non-normal."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus F-test is significant for any variable: Proceed with pairwise comparisons.",
    "Adjust for multiple comparisons using Tukey's HSD for balanced-like variance scenarios or Dunnett's test if comparing specifically against Sham as a control.",
    "If variances are heterogeneous (e.g., Success likely skewed, AD bounded), use Games-Howell post-hoc test.",
    "Effect size calculation: Compute Partial Eta-squared (ηp²) for all tests and Cohen's d for pairwise differences."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): The Sham group shows the lowest mean (0.236), suggesting higher dispersion (less efficient turning/stabilization) compared to others. Visual-only groups may differ from ICMS",
    "Success: The Sham group has a drastically lower mean success rate (0.273) compared to all other groups (>0.67), indicating ANOVA will likely be highly significant.",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham group has the highest mean (4.68), suggesting slower navigation compared to Combined (2.56) and ICMS (3.05).",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham group has the lowest efficiency (0.308) versus others (~0.43-0.50), suggesting less direct paths in Sham condition.",
    "Average Speed: Sham group is slower (~10.7) than Combined (~12.8), but differences appear smaller relative to their means compared to Success metrics."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe sample size imbalance: Combined (33x) and ICMS (3x) vs Sham may violate homoscedasticity assumptions for standard ANOVA.",
    "Bounded response variables: Success (0-1) and AD (0-1) may violate normality; Success is highly skewed.",
    "Path Efficiency interpretation: Some values (max 29.8) suggest it might not be a standard road-efficiency ratio (0-1), potentially invalidating direct comparison scales without standardization.",
    "Potential confounds: 'Sham' procedures may differ physiologically from 'Visual' or 'ICMS' in ways not captured by the ANOVA factor alone (e.g., surgical stress).",
    "Replication: Only Replication 2 is provided; conclusions cannot be generalized across biological replicates without data from other runs."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct Welch's ANOVA for all response variables to mitigate type I error due to unequal variances. For Success and AD, fit generalized linear models (binomial/quasi-binomial or beta regression) if normality assumptions fail despite transformation, followed by pairwise contrasts with bootstrap confidence intervals."
}
